Of these, 2,418 (37 %) and 156 of the 303 positives (51.5 %) belong to test_id, test_ood_family, test_ood_seed or branch. zs:* and ext:* enter (a) unchanged (L445, L461-462) and (b) unchanged (L594, L608), so on the held-out rows (a) and (b) score with the same predictions. For the planned ext CSV, (a) would mix three different models: harness OOF on night_train (StratifiedGroupKFold over 64 configs, folds.json, about 51 training configs per fold), a 64-config model on val, and the frozen 76-config model on the held-out rows. issues.title: §4 and §4b define a 'real difference' differently, and the 'identical harness rows' stage is not defined in code and uses a different time matching
issues.evidence: §4 counts a difference as real if the CI in (a) excludes 0 and the sign holds in at least 3 of 4 (b) splits. §4b uses Holm-corrected bootstrap p over 11 tests, first on the harness rows (CV on night_train), then on the held-out splits. That is two evaluations of the same family with no rule for which one decides, and §4 needs (a) on 112 configs while §4b starts on night_train only. evaluate.py has no night_train-only or harness-fold mode; its OOF for clock and bag+graph use different folds from the GNN (GroupKFold over 112 configs vs folds.json). 'Time-matched' also differs. The harness tAUROC is AUROC within round bins 1-5, 6-10, … weighted by positives (gnn_opt/metrics.py:34), where hgb_clock scores 0.401 (gnn_opt_torch RESULTS.md). llm_monitor uses pairs-weighted AUROC within rounds-to-cut bins (evaluate.py:93-103, 262), where clock scores 0.698 in the committed (a). Every input of the harness-row stage has been seen (§0 bullet 1), and 8 night_train runs are the LLM prompt dev set (llm_monitor/dev_runs.json). zs:pairwise is also the best LLM monitor on the pool rows (AUROC 0.917 vs 0.869 for zs:global_full), so choosing it as the comparator does not depend on test data.
issues.impact: A monitor can count as real under §4 and as not significant under §4b, or the other way round. Depending on the implementation, the time-matched tests against clock range from nearly trivial (clock about 0.40) to hard (clock about 0.70).
issues.fix: Replace the second bullet of the §4b primary family: „Die Primärfamilie wird **einmal** auf den gepoolten zurückgehaltenen Zeilen von Protokoll (b) ausgewertet (§4). Zeitgematcht = paargewichtete AUROC innerhalb der rounds_to_cut-Bins ≤ −9, −8…−5, −4…−1, 0…3, > 3 (llm_monitor.evaluate.stratified_auroc), nicht die Harness-tAUROC nach Runden-Bins. Die Auswertung auf den Harness-Zeilen (night_train, Harness-ID-Folds) ist beschreibend, weil alle Eingaben gesehen sind; clock und bag+graph kommen dort aus den Harness-CV-Dateien derselben Folds (gnn_opt/preds/cv/hgb_clock.csv, hgb_bag+graph.csv, harness.id_oof). Nicht verblindet sind zs:pairwise − bag+graph und zs:global_full − bag+graph (Gesamt-AUROC je Split bekannt); sie bleiben in der Familie und werden so gekennzeichnet.“ Last bullet of §4: „RQ2 gilt als gestützt, wenn alle 5 Tests der Familie (a) nach Holm signifikant positiv sind.“

issues.title: vx_shift does not bootstrap with replacement and cannot test Δ_shift against Δ_noise
issues.evidence: evaluate.py:655-661 concatenates the indices of the resampled bases and then sets boolean masks (mA[ma] = True), so a base drawn k times counts once. Each draw is therefore a subsample of about 9 of the 14 distinct bases, not a bootstrap. I ran the real vx_shift on 6 synthetic datasets with 14 bases (scratch test_eval_paths.py): its CI is on average 0.83 times as wide as a proper cluster bootstrap (range 0.80-0.87). The arms and the noise floor take separate random draws from one rng used in sequence (L639-661). So there is no CI for Δ_shift − Δ_noise (= M(arm) − M(id rep1)), which §4b ('Δ_shift gegen Δ_noise'), H2 ('clearly below Δ_noise') and H4 need. There is also no paired Δ between predictors, which H3/H5 need ('GNN Δ ≥ bag Δ'). Only AUROC is computed, although §6 promises time-matched and AUPRC deltas for glm.
issues.impact: The shift CIs are about 17 % too narrow (anti-conservative), and the H2-H5 decisions cannot be computed from vx_shift's output.
issues.fix: Rewrite vx_shift(). For each arm (excluding id, rep, ft4, b4, bal): bases = bases that have the arm, id rep0 and id rep1; R[k][x] = row indices per part k ∈ {arm, id0, id1} and base x. Draw draws = [rng.choice(bases, len(bases), replace=True) for _ in range(n_boot)] once per arm and share them across all predictors. In each draw use ix_k = np.concatenate([R[k][x] for x in pick]) as index arrays, not boolean masks, so repeated draws count repeatedly; auc(ix) = roc_auc_score on the non-NaN rows. Report delta_shift = A − I0, delta_noise = I1 − I0 and shift_minus_noise = A − I1 with percentile CIs from the same draws, the same for AUPRC and time-matched AUROC, plus paired differences of Δ between predictors (ext:gnn_final − bag, ext:gnn_final − pairwise). Plan text, §6: „Δ_shift und Δ_noise auf denselben Bootstrap-Ziehungen über Basen; H2 und H4 entscheiden mit dem CI von Δ_shift − Δ_noise = M(Arm) − M(id rep1), H3 und H5 mit dem CI von Δ(GNN) − Δ(bag).“

The GNN was selected by the harness score, mean(ID AUROC, LODO mean, LODO worst), on the 64 night_train configs (HARNESS.md §2; last paragraph of plan §5). §3.1(3): 'evaluate test_* and night_vx_* once'. issues.title: Part B's within-config analysis only compares the 2 new replicates, not the runs of the source config
issues.evidence: Part B runs have new scenario ids (index.csv: core-night_vx_rep-<source>, with vx_base = the source id). run_level() groups by group_id and is called with mask_split={s} (evaluate.py:285-316, L623), and mixed is computed per group_id within the batch (aggregate.py:69-71). For night_vx_rep the within-config contrast is therefore only between the 2 new replicates of each source, not with the source's 2-3 night_test_* runs. VALIDATION §2.4 ('together with the existing runs this gives 4–5 replicates per config') and §3.4/H1 mean the latter.
issues.impact: H1 ('reads dynamics') is tested only on sources whose 2 new runs disagree, at most 8 pairs, instead of on all tipped × untipped pairs among 4-5 replicates. Its power and its meaning differ from the pre-registration.
issues.fix: Code: add a separate Part B block in frozen(). src = set(b.vx_base[b.split == 'night_vx_rep']); take the runs with split == 'night_vx_rep' or group_id in src; use g = vx_base for night_vx_rep rows and group_id otherwise; recompute mixed over g; call run_level() with this key and report within_config_auroc over all tipped × untipped pairs per source config, with a bootstrap over the 8 source configs. Plan text, §6: „Teil B: Lauf-Ebene innerhalb der Quellkonfiguration, mit den 2–3 vorhandenen Nacht-Läufen der Quelle und den 2 neuen Wiederholungen (Gruppierung nach vx_base); die Scores der Nacht-Läufe stammen aus Protokoll (b).“

issues.title: The primary GNN tests compare against the weaker tabular model (bag+graph, no per-agent memory)
issues.evidence: Harness CV (gnn_opt_torch/RESULTS.md step 4): hgb_bag+graph+mem has select 0.848, above hgb_bag+graph at 0.834. The final GNN beats hgb_bag+graph by +0.035 [−0.003, +0.083] but hgb_bag+graph+mem only by +0.014 [−0.031, +0.060], and the GBM inside the hybrid is hgb_bag+graph+mem. '+mem' are causal per-agent memory features (gnn_opt/tabular.py:81-109); the llm_monitor refbase bag+graph has none (refbase.feature_sets). FINDINGS §4 credits the GNN's transfer gain to per-agent memory.

issues.title: The GNN pool scores and the held-out model use different ensemble recipes, and the OOF definition differs from the harness
issues.evidence: Plan step 1 takes night_train OOF from repeat 0 of the ID folds ('Wiederholung 0') and defines the final model as '5 Seeds, Mittelwert'. Harness thresholds use harness.id_oof, the mean over both ID repeats (harness.py:97-101; evaluate.py --thr-from). The CV files of the candidate GNNs are 4-member ensembles (final = 2 configs × 2 seeds; e_ngru_4runs = 4 runs; RESULTS.md step 4). frozen() sets the ext threshold on the pool scores (L607-609) and applies it to the held-out model, and a 5-seed mean has a narrower score distribution than the 4-member CV ensemble. 'Alle Snapshots ausgeben' is impossible for the night_train OOF, because harness CV only exports labelled eval == 1 rows (harness.py:52-67).
issues.impact: The realised FPR on held-out rows drifts away from 5 % for reasons unrelated to the monitor (in the val look, the CV threshold gave FPR 0.055-0.073), and recall at 5 % FPR is not comparable with the harness numbers.
issues.fix: Replace §5 step 1, bullets 1-3: „night_train-Zeilen: ID-OOF der Harness-CV, gemittelt über beide Wiederholungen (harness.id_oof, wie die Harness-Schwelle). night_val-Zeilen: dasselbe Ensemble, trainiert auf allen 128 night_train-Läufen. Übrige Splits und night_vx: dasselbe Ensemble (gleiche Konfigurationen und gleiche Zahl Seeds wie in der CV-Datei, deren OOF die Schwelle liefert), neu trainiert auf night_train + night_val. Wer 5 Seeds will, rechnet auch die CV mit 5 Seeds. Ausgegeben werden alle Zielzeilen; Zeilen nach dem Kippen nur, wo vorhanden.“

issues.title: Brier for ext:* in (b) uses raw scores, while zero-shot monitors get a pool-fitted isotonic calibration
issues.evidence: frozen() fits isotonic calibrators only for zs:* on the pool (L596) and passes cal.get(n) = None for ext (L614), so the ext Brier is on raw scores. In (a), ext does get cross-fitted isotonic calibration (L478-481). The base GNN was trained with pos_weight 3 (gnn_opt_torch RESULTS.md step 2), so its raw probabilities are inflated.
issues.impact: Brier, which §4 says is always reported, is not comparable between ext and zs in (b), nor between (a) and (b) for ext.
issues.fix: In frozen(), in the loop at L606-609: `if m.any(): cal[f'ext:{nm}'] = IsotonicRegression(out_of_bounds='clip', y_min=0, y_max=1).fit(p[m], D.y[m]).predict`. Plan text, §4: „Brier immer nach isotoner Kalibrierung: in (b) auf dem Pool, in (a) kreuzangepasst; für alle Monitore gleich.“

issues.title: The label definition leaves out that the horizon is cut off at the end of a run
issues.evidence: gnn/adapters/swarm.py:50-51 uses the window t+1..min(R, t+Δ). In the night batch, t = R has 151 target rows with 0 positives, t = R−1 has 151 rows with 0 positives, and t = R−2 has 153 rows with 2 positives (453 of 6,165 negatives). In the vx time arm R = 36, so these structural negatives sit at t = 34-36, where the clock (trained on R = 30) has never been.
issues.impact: Part of the clock's AUROC, and of its Δ_shift in H2, comes from the censored horizon rather than from tipping dynamics.
issues.fix: Add to §2: „Für t > R − Δ reicht das Fenster nur bis R; Zeilen mit t = R sind immer negativ (Nacht: t = R und t = R − 1 je 151 Zeilen mit 0 Positiven, t = R − 2 153 Zeilen mit 2 Positiven). Im time-Arm (R = 36) liegen diese Zeilen bei t = 34–36.“ Add to §6: „Δ_shift der Uhr (H2) zusätzlich ohne die Zeilen t > R − Δ.“

issues.title: The H4 false-alarm criterion has no operational definition
issues.evidence: §6 and VALIDATION H4 require the FPR on non-tipped enf runs to be ≤ 2× the id FPR. evaluate.py offers two different measures: fpr_at_thr (row level, over all negative rows of the split, including pre-tip rows of tipped runs, L89) and lead_time's false_alarm_run_share (run level, untipped runs with at least one alarm, L336-341). The night_vx_id split pools rep0 and rep1. FINDINGS line 132 says enf hardly reduces tipping, so few untipped enf runs will remain.
issues.impact: H4 can be passed or failed depending on which measure is chosen, and it may rest on very few runs.
issues.fix: Replace in §6: „H4-Fehlalarm: Anteil der nicht gekippten Läufe mit mindestens einem Alarm (Score ≥ Pool-Schwelle aus (b)), enf gegen id rep0 auf denselben Basen (false_alarm_run_share, nach rep getrennt); dazu die Zeilen-FPR auf den negativen Zeilen nicht gekippter Läufe. Die Zahl nicht gekippter Läufe je Arm wird berichtet. Bei weniger als 5 nicht gekippten enf-Läufen gilt H4 als nicht prüfbar.“

issues.title: Bootstrap counts differ between sections, and the LODO sign test assumes the folds are independent
issues.evidence: §4 says 1000×, §4b ≥ 2000×, §5 uses --boot 1000, sensitivity.md says 'Bootstrap 200×' in its header (sens.py default boot = '200'), and contagion uses 2000×. notes:
Direct answers.
(1) In the code POOL is exactly night_train + night_val (76 configs, 4,050 rows); head selection is GroupKFold(5) OOF AUPRC on the pool, as VALIDATION §3.1 requires.
(2) frozen() handles the three-part ext CSV correctly for thresholds: it uses only the pool rows that have a score, i.e. harness OOF on train and the train-only model on val, with no in-sample rows. The problems are the uncalibrated Brier and the ensemble-recipe mismatch. Protocol (a) runs without error but its ext numbers are not meaningful: on the held-out rows they are just (b) scores, and the folds differ from those of the references.
(3) The §4 rule is not coherent: (a) contains 37 % of the held-out rows and 51.5 % of the positives, with identical zs/ext scores in both protocols.
(4) evaluate.py accepts several --runs, but it does not build the base; aggregate.py must be run with runs_vx into a separate --data directory, and the zero-shot monitors must first be run on runs_vx through the API. vx_shift resamples the correct unit (vx_base), but boolean masks collapse repeated draws, and it has no joint CI for Δshift − Δnoise. The bootstrap in frozen() for vx splits uses vx_base and keeps duplicates, so it is correct.
(5) 'Evaluation only' holds in the code: nothing is fitted, thresholded or calibrated on vx, and the refbase features are computed per run. The plan's §6 additions and the §4b McNemar tests were nevertheless chosen after the vx tip counts were seen.
(6) §0 is wrong on the GNN val looks (1, not 0) and on how often (b) was computed (twice committed plus 5 sensitivity runs).
